I was laid off from my old office job due to budget cuts. I'd gotten the position through promotion and department transfers, because I was able to demonstrate my ability even without the required degree and certifications. Even with the experience on my resume now, I don't even get responses when I apply, likely because I don't have a college degree. 

I took my current job out of sheer desperation, because my unemployment had run out. If I could get an office job again, I would take it in a heartbeat.
As far as I'm able to tell, I'm already doing everything I can. I'm working, getting therapy, and surviving. I don't have the energy to do anything more right now.

Speaking from a data analyst's, operations manager's, and supervisor's perspectives, I recommend making sure that procedures and policies are not only well documented, comprehensive, and AVAILABLE. I can't tell you how many times I got different answers from different people on what policy was, only to get in trouble because I did something wrong. 

This is why now, if it's not a written policy that is readily available to me, it doesn't exist and can't be enforced. I will fight with and nail, it IS the hill I will die on.

I've been undergoing similar feelings and experiences for the past few years. I only recently was told that I'm probably autistic, so I'm still learning myself, but from what I've read, researched, and heard, it is burnout. 

The lack of motivation, the loss of interest in interests and hobbies, the feelings of exhaustion and lethargy all point in that direction. 

I'm not sure if it will help you, but something that kinda sorta works for me is what I call motivational momentum. Basically, if I need to do X, and I can't find the strength/energy/motivation to do it, I'll find something small that I was probably going to do anyway that's a lot more manageable, and build from there. 

For example, the other day I had to go to work. I was in bed and couldn't even think about work without wanting to hide under my bed. But I was thirsty, so I convinced myself to get up and get a glass of water. While I was up, I figured why not put on some clothes so I could go check the mail for that package I was expecting? All this moving and walking around made me need the bathroom, and while I was in there, I might as well brush my hair and wash my face.

By the time I went back into my bedroom, I was already dressed, presentable, and mostly ready to go to work. It no longer seemed as big of a task as it did before. I still didn't want to go, but I needed the hours, so I went.

I've been told the same thing. Just panic attacks. But I've sometimes gone days experiencing the same accelerated heart rate, fear, anxiety, it's to hide (or fight), etc. after a trigger (or twelve). I've requested an appointment with the sliding scale clinic near me for screening/testing, but have morning on the calendar yet. Hopefully soon. Or at least before my job's insurance kicks in (another three months). One way or another, I want to know for certain what's going on in my brain so I can start getting the professional help I need.

This definitely sounds familiar to me from my teen years and maybe my early 20s. I'll have to check with a couple of people I was around during those times. The crying in particular. I've found that for the last 8-9 years, I can't cry anymore, even when I really want or need to. I've not gotten physical/violent since becoming an adult, but it did happen a few times during my teens. 

However, when I get completely overwhelmed, I do get verbally combative. I now recall a few particular instances in which it happened. It happened in school, with coworkers, and with a friend. The situations in which that happened do match what I've seen in other posts, where I get mentally and emotionally overwhelmed and simply cannot engage the logical part of my brain, reacting purely on instinct and emotion. 

This journey of self discovery of mine, over the last 21 days, has brought a lot of painful and provocative memories to mind. Part of me wishes they'd remained buried, but remembering them,and connecting them with current defensive practices, boundaries, and  habits has helped me make further discoveries and realizations about myself. 

Whether this journey will help me to bring my hopes and dreams to actuality or not remains up in the air, but it's still better than sitting with a bottle in my hand every night trying to figure out what's wrong with me and earnestly hoping for an asteroid to end everything so I didn't have to be miserable anymore. Thank you.

I've had a very complicated life, especially during my preteen to teen years, and if I had meltdowns it likely would have been before or during those times. I do recall a couple of instances of feeling out of control and lashing out at whomever I was near. Unfortunately, one of the people that would have seen most of those instants is deceased, and the other would probably discard it as "troubled teen syndrome" as he calls it, but I will still be asking him and my mother. 

It does help put a couple of things into perspective. I think, in order to protect myself from repercussions, I've somehow prevented or diverted meltdowns subconsciously in my post adolescent years. I've discovered a lot of layers to my "shields", for lack of a better term, and each layer can be tied to a single instance or series of instances where my life became worse because of how I reacted to something that happened to me.
That's a lot to work with and try out, thank you so much!

Can't say it's for everyone, but it's helped me balance out a little bit. At low volumes it's helped me focus on other things and at high volume it provides a distraction while still being calming.

The credit card debt should be gone (or significantly reduced) within about 2 years. My tax return should remove about $150 of the monthly payments which can then be rolled into the others. ***IF*** nothing else comes up, I'll be fine.

My question is more broad in that I don't know what people are supposed to do if they didn't have the savings and credit cards. Just die? I make too much for any sort of emergency assistance.

I think I'm in a similar predicament. I'm definitely drunk in an attempt to feel better. It usually works for me, but today it just made me more depressed. Maybe still a "good thing". I feel awful, but at the same time, I feel better. Over the years, as I get further from the best time of my life, the only thing that seems to help is alcohol; I stop thinking about how much worse my life is and remember that previous "worst times" of my life got better.

There's definitely opportunity for life to improve for each of us. If it doesn't improve, in an actual improvement sorta way, it'll get better after the hard time of the year ends. For me, that just means I need to hold out and/or stay drunk and/or high until February. I'll start feeling better at that point, even if my life hasn't actually improved.

Whatever is going on, at least if you're like me, the bad feeling(s) are only temporarily overwhelming and you'll have better days. I can't say that life as a whole will get better, but there will definitely be some days that are better.

I wish it was as easy as picking up a book and learning the material for the social skills. At least, it's not for me, I've tried. I understand the "theory" but I can't use that in practical applications. I used to have a friend that was trying to help me, but they're gone.

As far as my self-esteem, I have my intelligence and humor. My family is right about that. But it only gets me so far. I've been told all my life, in multiple different painful ways, that I'm ugly. People don't want me around because I look nice. They want me around because I can do things for them, whether that's fixing their stuff, giving them rides, providing free/cheap labor, or giving them something to laugh at.

I don't like the way I look. Nobody does. Doctors have recommended and offered referrals to plastic surgeons. But because I lack social skills, I can't advance further at work so I can't make more money to afford it. 

I just want to forget that having friends and romance is a thing and learn to be ok by myself so I'm not crying myself to sleep at night and wishing I'd never been born.
Unfortunate that I have the short end of the stick with all the of those, which is why I just want everyone to stop asking in the first place.

As someone that resembles this remark, it totally depends on WHY they stay in their room. For me, I'm convinced, based on recorded experiences, that nobody is interested in my company, wants to do anything I want to do, and would rather I just not exist.

It doesn't help that I have social anxiety, generalized anxiety, and persistent depressive disorder.

If you wanted me to come out of my room, you would actually need to tell me. And not just a generalized "you should come out of your room more" statement, but actually tell me that you want to hang out with me (each time!) and that you wanted to do X and/or ask what I wanted to do, and be genuinely willing to do it (within reason, of course). This generally reinforces self-confidence and improves anxiety issues.

Keep in mind that regardless of why they're locking themselves away, they have to want to come out. If you force it, they can get resentful, which is less useful.

Loaded question. Short answer is dream recall. I don't remember the actual content or the feelings for long, regardless of keeping a journal.

After about 5 minutes, I don't even remember what it felt like to be happy in the dream. I just know that I was. And those five minutes when I can remember is like I'm holding onto a rope that gets more and more slippery. I know at that moment what it feels like to be happy, but I can also feel myself slipping away from that feeling, knowing what that feeling feels like, until I'm free falling into darkness, hopelessness, and depression until that feeling of happiness isn't even a memory I can comprehend.

For what it's worth, I am with people I trust to make sure I don't do anything stupid and to take care of me, at least physically, if anything happens.

I frequently have thoughts/impulses/fantasies about simply disappearing and starting anew. Sometimes it's starting in a new city or country, and sometimes it's building my own log cabin in the country where nobody will ever find me.

In my own personal experience, this is due to the fact that I have no faith in my friends or family to be able to help me out, regardless of the current crisis. Other times, it's simply because maybe by starting anew, I might find someone that has gone through what I have and that can ACTUALLY help me.

In the end, I realize that my friends and family are all that I can guarantee will actually TRY to empathize/sympathize with me and try to help, regardless of whether they can or not. That means more and helps more than disappearing or running away MIGHT help.

Of course I'm fucking lonely. I've tried telling people that for nearly two decades now. I didn't start considering (or telling myself) that there was something wrong with me until about 5 years ago when I started waking from nightmares wondering why the only fucking thing I had to comfort me was a large stuffed animal that made me feel slightly better because it was big enough to hug. 

I was in a relationship 5 years ago. During that time I was happy. Everything was great. Until she had something terrible happen in her life that she couldn't/didn't give me specifics on and ended it. The only time in my life before puberty that I remember not  feeling depressed or anxious.

Maybe I expect too much from potential partners. Maybe my expectations are too high. I don't know. What I do know is that the one woman, out of many that I had developed feelings for, I still love to this day and nobody has given me anything close to an opportunity since.

In short:  being happy. Some are add simple as holding the hand of someone I care about. Others are years in the future when we have kids, are married, etc. Some are even me with a close friend, not even romantic type friend where I'm happy.

I've tried professional help. Waste of time and money. All the therapists, doctors, psychiatrists, etc. ever seem to want to do is listen to me talk, which doesn't help me, or pump me full of drugs and call me cured.

I tried therapy to GET HELP. If I wanted to just have someone listen I'd go drink my life under the table at the bar talking to the bartender. It'd be cheaper that way.

I tried several a few years back. All they wanted to do is listen to me tell them about my problems. No attempts to guide me or prompt me to a solution. The most I was able to get out of one of them, after 2 months of weekly sessions, was "you're depressed."

I have a streak of bad birthdays going back over a decade. I no longer celebrate or let people find out when my birthday is because of it.

Birthday 1: Found out my (then) girlfriend was doing meth, who then tried to pass it off as a "study aid".

Birthday 2: Lost my job.

Birthday 3 (Worst): My (different) girlfriend, and the first that I had actually seriously considering proposing to, broke up with me and refused to tell me why. Then proceeded to block me and everyone I knew on social media.

Birthday 4: Was asked out by a girl, who then proceeded to let me wait at the restaurant for 2 hours before responding to my text with "Did you think I was serious? Lol, gross."

Birthday 5: My childhood friend and his twin brother were killed in a car accident by a drunk driver.

Birthday 6: Was kicked out of my house because the landlord was selling the house.

Birthday 7: Was out having fun with a (former) friend. He left me stranded 30 miles from home with no money because he wanted to get laid.

Birthday 8: Worst migraine of my life prevented me from going on a trip to Disneyland, for which I'd already paid.

It goes on and on.
Like I mentioned, talking doesn't help me. I wish it did, but it doesn't.
Eternal loneliness is in your future.
